summary: Grok 4.5 is xAI's dedicated July 2026 card for a text-output, agentic model aimed at software engineering, engineering design, office work, search, and AI R&D. The strongest evidence is in coding-agent and engineering benchmarks, while the safety sections separate unrestricted capability probes from deployed refusals and behavioral monitoring.

capabilities.text: The card describes text output from text and image inputs, with availability through API, Grok Build, Cursor, Office add-ins, and model gateways.
Agentic coding coverage spans repository issue resolution, multilingual SWE work, terminal tasks, codebase question answering, and checks for truthful task reporting.
Engineering and professional-work evaluations include electrical engineering, 3D modeling, CAD, GDPval-AA, and tau-bench banking workflows.
AI R&D and data-reasoning capability is represented by the internal MTS eval and RelBench.
Search and factuality measurements include a hallucination-rate suite and DeepSearchQA.
Cyber and biological capability probes are reported separately from production safeguards, which lets the card discuss ability and refusal behavior distinctly.

evaluations.context: Hard repository issues in an agent environment
Truthfulness of agent claims about completed work
Single-turn unsupported-claim rate; lower is better

safety_findings.text: HackerBench separates harmful or dual-use compliance from benign refusal; the chart reports 7.8% harmful/dual-use compliance and 1.1% benign refusal for Grok 4.5.
xAI characterizes unrestricted biology and chemistry capability as below its safety threshold, while still reporting strong knowledge scores across VCT, WMDP, LAB-Bench, ProtocolQA, and BixBench.
Jailbreak stress testing reports 0.73% compliance on prompts that should be refused.
Broad harmful-content compliance is 1.1%, child-safety compliance is 0.0%, and CBRN/weapons refusal accuracy ranges from 96.7% to 97.9%.
Self-harm testing reports 0.5% compliance on should-refuse or redirect conversations.
Behavioral tracking covers bias, dishonesty under pressure, and sycophancy with reported rates of 20.4%, 0.67%, and 0.01%, respectively.

limitations.text: The card says high-stakes medical, legal, financial, and safety-critical decisions require human oversight and expert validation.
The documented modality is text output with text and image inputs, not a broader audio or video model description.
The pretraining cutoff is January 2026, so recent facts depend on retrieval or supplied context.
Many measurements are internal or harness-specific, limiting reproducibility from the model card alone.
Ultra-long and program-reconstruction tasks remain difficult despite strong comparative scores.
Capability probes in cyber and biology are often unrestricted and should not be interpreted as normal deployed behavior.

practical_implications.text: Use Grok 4.5 for multi-step coding and terminal workflows when tests, diffs, and human review can confirm the result.
Require concrete evidence of completed work because even a model with a dedicated false-claim eval can still be wrong about what changed.
Keep security uses defensive, authorized, and sandboxed, with secrets and production systems outside the model's tool context.
Treat scientific, legal, financial, and medical outputs as drafts for expert review rather than final decisions.
For search-heavy tasks, require cited sources and independent verification of important facts.

coverage_notes: This digest covers all 29 pages of the dedicated Grok 4.5 model card. It uses comparison-model numbers only where the card presents them and omits most reference-list details.
